newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks sharply rebound over Iraq prospects.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks sharply rebound over Iraq prospects.

text.p: Jordanian stocks on Saturday rose to their highest levels in nine months on optimism for a revival of trade with Iraq once the delayed U.N. oil-for-food deal is implemented.

Investors said resumed active buying across-the-board was fueled by the chance for trade revival with Jordan's biggest trading partner. The U.N. deal to let Iraq sell $2 billion of oil over six months moved closer to implementation when Iraq in November said it accepted all the conditions.

"The market's strong showing maybe be a prelude for better things to come once Iraq does finally begin to sell oil," said Omar al-Masri, head of Atlas Investment Group, a financial consultancy specialising in regional emerging markets.
Many firms have still not made up for the loss of the Iraqi market in 1990 when economic sanctions were imposed on Baghdad after it invaded Kuwait.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose to its highest level since March to 152.89 points in trade worth 2.6 million dinars ($3.6 million), nearly three-fold its recent average.
The bourse's 1.89 percent rise on Saturday was the highest one day jump since last April's short rally triggered by government instigated buying by state pesnion funds.

Most of the key bluechip industrials that export basic humanitarian goods to Iraq saw sharp rises to the maximum five percent limit in one trading session, with brokers saying there was healthy across-the-board demand.
The firms that posted highest rises were Jordan Selpho-Chemicals, Arab Paper Converting Trading and Union Chemical and Vegetable, all with five percent rises. The firms all export to Iraq.
Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturers also rose by 0.16 dinars to 3.44 dinars with optimism pharmaceutical firms will benefit from Iraqi purchases of urgently needed medicines.
Industrial firms, some of which sell goods like detergents not covered by the tough U.N. sanctions, also see the oil-for-food deal as a firm step towards the full lifting of the embargo.
Gaining shares outnumbered losers on Saturday by 46 to four, with another three trading but closing unchanged.
